# Phase 5 prompt — Implement the idea-aware tool recommendation engine

Implement only Phase 5 of the Unfinished Business roadmap. Add transparent, idea-specific recommendations for open-source, free-tier, and promotional hackathon tools. Do not automatically install tools or turn the product into a sponsor directory.

## Prerequisite

Verify the project section model and Tools & Budget section from Phase 3 are stable. The recommendation UI must use the visual system from Phase 4 and must not bypass Architect approval.

## Outcome

Given an approved idea and constraints, the product recommends a small, ranked set of relevant tools with an honest explanation of fit, license, cost/free limit, integration effort, privacy/lock-in concerns, and challenge relevance. Users can add recommendations to the plan, reject them, or defer them.

## Data and policy work

- Create a versioned tool-catalog schema containing: tool ID/name, categories, capabilities, open-source/open-weight/proprietary status, license, self-host option, free tier or promotional status, material limits, setup mode, likely effort, privacy/lock-in notes, official sources, last verified date, and status such as core/conditional/promo-only/excluded.
- Seed the catalog with every tool requested by the product owner:
  - Render, TabPFN, Tinker, Arduino, DigitalOcean, Gemma, Auth0 for AI Agents, Backboard, ElevenLabs, Browserbase/Stagehand, Entire, GitHub Copilot, Mastra, MongoDB Atlas, Ultramarine, Sentry Agent Tracing, SerpApi, `.tech` domain, Temporal, and Tiger Data.
- Also include OpenCode, Ollama, SQLite, Playwright, axe-core, OpenTelemetry, Mermaid, and GitHub Actions where relevant.
- Use official current sources for facts that may change. Store a last-verified date and avoid hard-coded claims that cannot be maintained.
- Distinguish clearly:
  - open source;
  - open weight with a separate model license;
  - self-hosted free software;
  - proprietary free tier;
  - trial/promotional credit;
  - paid-only or hardware-cost-dependent.
- Never treat trial credit as permanent free usage.

## Recommendation logic

- Extract or accept structured project needs: web, AI inference, fine-tuning, tabular data, hardware, voice, browser automation, authentication, search, durable workflows, time-series/telemetry, remote database, vector search, and public deployment.
- Implement deterministic rules/scoring first. Model-generated explanations may refine wording but cannot invent cost, license, quota, or compatibility facts.
- Return a small ranked result with `why`, `why not`, prerequisites, effort, limitations, and a fallback.
- Respect explicit constraints: no spending, local-only, open-source-only, deadline, privacy, hardware availability, and existing stack.
- Do not recommend a tool solely because it sponsors a challenge.
- Keep OpenCode as the only harness. Exclude Copilot as a runtime alternative; keep Mastra/Backboard conditional for applications built by the user, not internal orchestration.
- Require user approval before adding a recommendation to the project plan. Adding it does not install, create an account, claim a credit, deploy, or authorize spending.
- Show a stale-data warning when catalog facts exceed the verification policy.

## Initial policy expectations

- Core for this product: OpenCode, Entire, Sentry; Render only under the documented mode/cost constraints.
- Strong local/open choices when the idea fits: Gemma/Ollama, SQLite, Playwright, axe-core, OpenTelemetry, Mermaid, Temporal self-hosted, and relevant Tiger Data components.
- Conditional: TabPFN, Arduino, Auth0, ElevenLabs, Stagehand/Browserbase, MongoDB Atlas, SerpApi, Mastra.
- Promotional rather than default-free: Tinker, DigitalOcean credits, Backboard credits, Ultramarine offers, and `.tech` domain.
- GitHub Copilot remains excluded from product harness choices.

Verify all classifications during implementation; these expectations are not a substitute for current official evidence.

## Tests

Add table-driven tests for common idea profiles, explicit exclusions, no-budget/local-only constraints, stale catalog data, conflicting tools, unsupported claims, stable ordering, approval/defer/reject flow, and safe serialization. Include a regression that an OpenCode-only project is never advised to switch harnesses.

## Documentation requirements

Update:

- `docs/TOOL_CATALOG.md` with the complete catalog, sources, verification date, classification policy, and maintenance procedure;
- `docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md` for user value and recommendation boundaries;
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for catalog/rules/model boundaries;
- `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` for recommendation cards, filters, warnings, and approval states;
- `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md` for optional local dependencies only when selected;
- `docs/HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md` for hosting implications;
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, and `README.md`.

Do not place volatile prices only in prose; keep a clearly maintained source/date structure. Do not claim a challenge category without meaningful implemented usage and evidence.

## Acceptance

- Every requested tool is classified with source/date and honest free/open/promo status.
- Recommendations change based on the idea and constraints.
- Explanations are deterministic enough to test and never invent commercial facts.
- No recommendation performs an external action.
- OpenCode remains the only harness.
- The catalog and UI agree; typecheck, tests, and build pass.

Finish with the required phase handoff and stop. Do not start Phase 6.

1: # Unfinished Business
2: 
3: **Bring your ideas to life.**
4: 
5: A local browser companion built on OpenCode's open-source coding harness. Four friendly spirits guide a builder from an unfinished idea through an approved plan, real implementation, verification, and submission drafts.
6: 
7: | Spirit | Role |
8: |---|---|
9: | Oracle | Clarify an idea and approve a useful product scope |
10: | Architect | Present one planning section, revise it, and wait for approval before continuing |
11: | Maker | Use OpenCode to perform approved work and show actual results |
12: | Witness | Review evidence and prepare honest final materials |
13: 
14: OpenCode provides the agent loop, model access, tools, permissions, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the workshop interface, stage progression, versioned approvals, decision history, and evidence views.
15: 
16: ## Status
17: 
18: Prompt 2 is active. Foundation is `14fc6a6`, Workflow is `abf87f7`, and Experience is `b465fa0`. The Verification phase has entered local reconciliation: typecheck, production build, all 21 tests, and the production dependency audit pass. Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness run through OpenCode's free DeepSeek route. Maker edits only an isolated demo workspace, then the app runs `node --test` there. A live umbrella-relay attempt wrote a ledger whose Node check failed on a duplicate `snapshot` declaration; Witness recorded that failure. Sentry error, performance, replay, feedback, profiling, and metadata-only OpenCode agent tracing are verified locally. Backboard remains dependent on its API/tooling setup.
19: 
20: ```bash
21: npm ci
22: npm run dev

55: Primary user: a first-time hackathon builder or developer using AI who struggles with what to ask, which tool capability to choose, how to carry decisions between sessions, and how to know when the result is actually ready.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How does billing work?

Render charges for three things: your workspace plan (flat subscription), metered features like bandwidth (usage-based), and [compute](https://render.com/pricing#compute) for your applications (usage-based). 

### How am I billed for compute?

[Compute plans](https://render.com/pricing#compute) are set at a per-service basis, and billing is prorated to the second. If you create a web service on a paid compute plan and turn it off 24 hours later, you are only billed for 24 hours of compute. This also applies to service types that spin up and shut down automatically, like Cron Jobs and Workflows. You are only billed for compute when these services are actively running your workload.

### My Pro or Scale workspace did not have any activity or services this month. Will I still be charged for the workspace subscription? 

If a workspace has no services (live or suspended) and no activity during a month, the workspace subscription fee for that month will be waived.

### I run a large agency with developers on multiple teams. What does this mean for us?

Scale and Enterprise plans let you create multiple workspaces within the same organization to better manage multiple teams. Our team is happy to help you determine the best way to organize your teams on Render. [Contact us](https://render.com/contact) here.

### What are build pipeline minutes, and how can I track my usage?

Your workspace's builds and other pre-deploy tasks use Render compute resources. [Pipeline minutes](https://docs.render.com/build-pipeline#pipeline-minutes) track the duration of these tasks. You can view your pipeline usage from your dashboard's Billing page.

With a Professional plan or higher, you can enable the [Performance pipeline](https://docs.render.com/build-pipeline#pipeline-tiers) to run builds on larger compute instances, with an additional corresponding charge for pipeline minutes.

### How do free compute plans work?

With Render’s [Free compute plans](https://render.com/docs/free), you can spin up [web services](https://docs.render.com/free#free-web-services), [Render Key Value instances](https://docs.render.com/free#free-key-value), and [Render Postgres databases](https://render.com/docs/free#free-postgres) at no charge. Free compute plans types have usage limits and are designed to help you to explore new tech, build personal projects, and preview Render's developer experience.

### Which payment methods do you accept?

We accept all major credit and debit cards. Your payment info is stored and processed securely by [Stripe](https://stripe.com/) and never touches our servers.

### Why was I charged $1 after adding a credit card?

A $1 USD transaction is performed as a credit security check to ensure your card details are correct and authorized. The charge is refunded after the transaction completes.

### We are migrating infrastructure from another provider. Can Render provide professional services to handle the migration?

Render does not offer full migration professional services. However, you can find a certified solution partner through our [expert network](https://render.com/experts).

### I have an infrequently asked question.

Great! We're always around to help. You can email us any time at [support@render.com](mailto:support@render.com), or talk to us in our [user community](https://community.render.com/).

# BIG ANNOUNCEMENT! WE’RE COMING TO ISLAMABAD! | Ultramarine Tech · LinkedIn · 2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00

**Ultramarine Tech**.

parts.text:
Now, the task requires web research for "official current sources for facts that may change." I should use websearch/webfetch to verify tool classifications. But this environment may or may not have network. Let's test quickly. We need every requested tool classified with source/date and honest free/open/promo status. The catalog should have official source URLs and lastVerified date. I can use today's date 2026-10-31 (environment says Sat Oct 31 2026). But I need current facts. Let me attempt web searches for key tools. Since many are fictional/future (Backboard, Entire, Tinker, Ultramarine, Entire), I'll rely on known info and official sources with careful classification, marking uncertainty.

Given the scope, this is a big implementation. Let me plan the architecture:

1. `src/shared/tool-catalog.ts` or `src/server/recommendations/catalog.ts` — typed catalog with version, tools, metadata, sources, lastVerified. Keep serializable, sanitize.
2. `src/server/recommendations/needs.ts` — extract structured needs from idea text; explicit constraints parsing (no-spend, local-only, open-source-only, deadline, privacy, hardware, existing stack).
3. `src/server/recommendations/rules.ts` — deterministic scoring/ranking; returns ranked results with why/whyNot/prerequisites/effort/limitations/fallback, policy statuses, stale warning.
4. `src/server/recommendations/service.ts` — orchestration, approvals/defer/reject persisted in project, recommendation action records. Could be integrated with workflow model.

Data model additions:
- recommendation state in project: `recommendations: Array<{ id (toolId), status: "RECOMMENDED"|"ADDED"|"DEFERRED"|"REJECTED", reason, decidedAt, ideaFingerprint? }>`; maybe store per-tool decision. Better: `toolDecisions` in project. Add schema version bump? Project schemaVersion 1 literal. We need backwards compatibility with old stored projects. We can add defaults to new fields keeping schemaVersion 1. That's easiest and safe; the prompt says "safe serialization". Add `.default([])`. 

- Need "Tools & Budget" section model stable. Existing section "tools" title "Tools, access, and cost". We'll use it as anchor, perhaps render recommendations when stage architect and section id "tools", plus in witness. Prompt says "Verify the project section model and Tools & Budget section from Phase 3 are stable." We can rely on section `tools` and add recommendation UI triggered during architect tools section and maybe a dedicated always-available panel. Need to not bypass architect approval. Decisions are separate from section approval; "Add to plan" should add a section? Actually "add recommendations to the plan" - production plan is approved sections. To not bypass Architect approval, adding a tool should not modify approved section content. Instead, add to "selected tools" list that is included in export as an appendix and subject to a separate approval? The requirement: "Require user approval before adding a recommendation to the project plan. Adding it does not install..." So the user approves adding a recommendation; that's an explicit action. It can append to project.selectedTools and contribute a "Tools & Budget" addendum, but not mutate approved section content. To preserve Architect approval, we can require the tools section to be approved or record that tool selection won't alter approved sections; adding shows in plan export as a separately-approved addendum. Better design:

- Recommendations are advisory; decisions are recorded with status ADDED only on explicit user action.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How does billing work?

Render charges for three things: your workspace plan (flat subscription), metered features like bandwidth (usage-based), and [compute](https://render.com/pricing#compute) for your applications (usage-based). 

### How am I billed for compute?

[Compute plans](https://render.com/pricing#compute) are set at a per-service basis, and billing is prorated to the second. If you create a web service on a paid compute plan and turn it off 24 hours later, you are only billed for 24 hours of compute. This also applies to service types that spin up and shut down automatically, like Cron Jobs and Workflows. You are only billed for compute when these services are actively running your workload.

### My Pro or Scale workspace did not have any activity or services this month. Will I still be charged for the workspace subscription? 

If a workspace has no services (live or suspended) and no activity during a month, the workspace subscription fee for that month will be waived.

### I run a large agency with developers on multiple teams. What does this mean for us?

Scale and Enterprise plans let you create multiple workspaces within the same organization to better manage multiple teams. Our team is happy to help you determine the best way to organize your teams on Render. [Contact us](https://render.com/contact) here.

### What are build pipeline minutes, and how can I track my usage?

Your workspace's builds and other pre-deploy tasks use Render compute resources. [Pipeline minutes](https://docs.render.com/build-pipeline#pipeline-minutes) track the duration of these tasks. You can view your pipeline usage from your dashboard's Billing page.

With a Professional plan or higher, you can enable the [Performance pipeline](https://docs.render.com/build-pipeline#pipeline-tiers) to run builds on larger compute instances, with an additional corresponding charge for pipeline minutes.

### How do free compute plans work?

With Render’s [Free compute plans](https://render.com/docs/free), you can spin up [web services](https://docs.render.com/free#free-web-services), [Render Key Value instances](https://docs.render.com/free#free-key-value), and [Render Postgres databases](https://render.com/docs/free#free-postgres) at no charge. Free compute plans types have usage limits and are designed to help you to explore new tech, build personal projects, and preview Render's developer experience.

### Which payment methods do you accept?

We accept all major credit and debit cards. Your payment info is stored and processed securely by [Stripe](https://stripe.com/) and never touches our servers.

### Why was I charged $1 after adding a credit card?

A $1 USD transaction is performed as a credit security check to ensure your card details are correct and authorized. The charge is refunded after the transaction completes.

### We are migrating infrastructure from another provider. Can Render provide professional services to handle the migration?

Render does not offer full migration professional services. However, you can find a certified solution partner through our [expert network](https://render.com/experts).

### I have an infrequently asked question.

Great! We're always around to help. You can email us any time at [support@render.com](mailto:support@render.com), or talk to us in our [user community](https://community.render.com/).

Training loop

1. **Sample responses**

   Your code sends prompts from the current batch. Tinker’s samplers generate responses using the current sampling snapshot and return them to your loop.

2. **Compute gradients**

   Your code evaluates the responses and computes rewards, then sends the training batch to Tinker. Its training GPUs compute and accumulate gradients without changing the weights.

3. **Update the weights**

   On Tinker’s training GPUs, the optimizer applies accumulated gradients to your trainable weights.

4. **Save progress**

   When you choose to checkpoint, Tinker stores weights and optimizer state so you can resume later. You choose how often to save.

5. **Refresh samplers and repeat**

   Your code refreshes Tinker’s samplers with a snapshot of the updated weights, selects the next batch, and repeats. Later training leaves the snapshot unchanged. This is one example loop; you choose when to save and refresh weights.

Generate tokens for chat, evaluation, or RL rollouts.

### forward\_backward

Run a forward and backward pass and accumulate the gradient.

### optim\_step

Update trainable weights based on the accumulated gradient.

## FAQs

How do I access Tinker?

Join [here](https://auth.thinkingmachines.ai/sign-up). If you’re a university or organization looking for wide scale access, contact [\[email protected\]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#73071a1d18160133071b1a1d181a1d141e12101b1a1d16005d121a).

What is LoRA and why does Tinker use it?

LoRA is an efficient approach to fine-tuning that trains a streamlined adapter instead of updating all base model weights. Our [research](/blog/lora/) demonstrates that with the right setup, LoRA matches the learning performance of full fine-tuning while providing more flexibility and requiring less compute.

What do I need to start training?

A dataset of supervised learning examples or reinforcement learning environments. After picking a base model to train on, the Tinker API provides simple functions to compute gradients, update the weights, and sample outputs from the trained model. See our cookbook for examples to get started.

Can I download my model weights?

Yes, we have an API endpoint that lets you download any checkpoint you’ve saved.

How do I stay up to date with Tinker news?

[Follow Tinker on X](https://x.com/tinkerapi) for API updates, new model and feature announcements, and weekly roundups of featured projects from the Tinker community. ## Frequently asked questions

### How do I give AI agents the right permissions without hardcoding?

Hardcoding permissions is fast, but it fragments control and slows scale. [Auth0 lets agents](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/user-authentication) act more securely on behalf of users with centralized authorization. Policies evolve without code changes, and each action is auditable.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/call-your-apis-on-users-behalf)

### Can I treat AI agents like regular users?

Not exactly. Agents act continuously and across multiple systems on behalf of many users. Roles multiply, accountability blurs, and traceability becomes tricky. Auth0 provides patterns for modelling agents distinctly, so each action is intentional and auditable.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/asynchronous-authorization)

### What happens if authorization lives outside the identity layer?

Authorization in downstream services or app code works temporarily but fails at scale. Every new capability increases surface area and drift. Auth0 centralizes authorization in the identity layer, keeping policies consistent, adaptive, and auditable.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/get-started/authorization-for-rag)

### How does Auth0 help move AI agents from pilot to production?

By combining secure identity, [fine-grained authorization](https://auth0.com/fine-grained-authorization), and centralized control, Auth0 enables agents to act safely and autonomously at scale. Teams ship faster, reduce rework, and gain confidence in every deployment.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/overview)

### Can Auth0 integrate with my existing systems and APIs?

Yes. Auth0 works with any AI agent or application that makes API calls, including first-party APIs, external services, and third-party AI platforms. Integration is seamless and maintains auditability across your stack.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/get-started/overview)

### How does Auth0 help ensure AI agents comply with privacy and security standards?

AI agents often handle sensitive user data, making compliance critical. Auth0 enforces fine-grained authorization, audit trails, and identity verification for agent actions, helping you meet your regulatory requirements like GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/docs/secure/data-privacy-and-compliance)

### Can AI agents securely access multiple applications or APIs?

Yes. Auth0 enables cross-app and cross-service access for AI agents while enforcing centralized policies. Agents can request only the data and actions they need, reducing risk and maintaining traceable, auditable access across your stack.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/call-others-apis-on-users-behalf)

### How do I scale AI agent deployments without increasing security risk?

Scaling agents can quickly increase your attack surface if authorization isn’t centralized. Auth0 moves identity and permissions into the [platform](https://auth0.com/platform) so that new agents can onboard quickly, policies can evolve automatically, and teams can retain complete oversight and auditability.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/get-started/overview)

Training loop

1. **Sample responses**

   Your code sends prompts from the current batch. Tinker’s samplers generate responses using the current sampling snapshot and return them to your loop.

2. **Compute gradients**

   Your code evaluates the responses and computes rewards, then sends the training batch to Tinker. Its training GPUs compute and accumulate gradients without changing the weights.

3. **Update the weights**

   On Tinker’s training GPUs, the optimizer applies accumulated gradients to your trainable weights.

4. **Save progress**

   When you choose to checkpoint, Tinker stores weights and optimizer state so you can resume later. You choose how often to save.

5. **Refresh samplers and repeat**

   Your code refreshes Tinker’s samplers with a snapshot of the updated weights, selects the next batch, and repeats. Later training leaves the snapshot unchanged. This is one example loop; you choose when to save and refresh weights.

Generate tokens for chat, evaluation, or RL rollouts.

### forward\_backward

Run a forward and backward pass and accumulate the gradient.

### optim\_step

Update trainable weights based on the accumulated gradient.

### save\_state

Save weights and optimizer state so you can resume training later.

What is LoRA and why does Tinker use it?

LoRA is an efficient approach to fine-tuning that trains a streamlined adapter instead of updating all base model weights. Our [research](/blog/lora/) demonstrates that with the right setup, LoRA matches the learning performance of full fine-tuning while providing more flexibility and requiring less compute.

What do I need to start training?

A dataset of supervised learning examples or reinforcement learning environments. After picking a base model to train on, the Tinker API provides simple functions to compute gradients, update the weights, and sample outputs from the trained model. See our cookbook for examples to get started.

Can I download my model weights?

# Ship AI agents, not identity work

Your next competitive advantage is built on AI—not on rebuilding the identity layer. Offload the identity work, so your dev team can focus on shipping agents faster.

- [Explore the guide](https://auth0.com/resources/whitepapers/from-prototype-to-production)

## Builders’ paradox: Agents get more advanced, but your team’s velocity slows.

### 3-5 months
The average time that is added to an AI agent’s deployment timeline due to security reviews and the implementation of identity guardrails.
[RAND Corporation](https://www.rand.org/content/dam/rand/pubs/research_reports/RRA2600/RRA2680-1/RAND_RRA2680-1.pdf)

### €1-2 million
The estimated maintenance cost over five years for a self-built [authentication]( https://auth0.com/platform/authentication) system.
[GitNation](https://gitnation.com/contents/auth-build-vs-open-source-vs-buy)

### 88%
of AI agent projects never make it out of the pilot phase and into production. The top cited reasons aren’t “bad AI”, but integration complexity and identity governance.
[Lenovo](https://www.lenovo.com/us/en/solutions/cioplaybook2026/)

## Remove identity work from the   critical path

As agents get deployed more widely, the auth work around them grows quickly. Here’s how Auth0 helps organizations from slowing down.

### Offload identity infrastructure
*Go from maintenance to innovation*
Your best engineers are likely rebuilding identity for every new AI pilot. Standardizing it in one place removes that repetitive work, so your team can focus on the core product.
[Learn how](https://auth0.com/resources/whitepapers/developer-blueprint-for-production-ready-apps-and-ai-agents)

### Enable high-value interactions
*Enable agents to do more, faster*
As AI agents move to executing actions on behalf of human users, teams end up building one-off integrations that don’t scale. Define permissions once and apply them across multiple systems.
[Learn how](https://auth0.com/resources/whitepapers/from-prototype-to-production)

### Scale without repeated rework
*Stop rebuilding identity for each new release*
When identity is handled in one place, teams don’t have to revisit it with each new release. Keep your dev team focused and moving without repeat work.
[Learn how](https://auth0.com/resources/webinars/auth0-streamcast-episode-2)

## Why leaders choose Auth0

Each new feature leads to more edge cases, logic, and identity work to maintain. Auth0 moves that work out of your code and into a centralized layer, so you define it once and reuse it across multiple [features](https://auth0.com/features) or edge cases.

## Build and scale AI   experiences in your industry

### Stop losing customers to checkout friction
Fragmented identity kills conversion and loyalty. Auth0 enables adaptive [authentication](https://auth0.com/platform/authentication) and fine-grained authorization across touchpoints without custom work.
[Learn more](https://auth0.com/retail)
- Convert traffic without sacrificing fraud controls
- Authorize pricing agents and personalized offers
- Deliver personalized commerce at scale

### Support complex actions without slowing delivery
Hardcoded rules and fragmented systems don’t scale with automation. Auth0 ties each transaction (human or AI-driven) to verified identity with built-in audit trails and compliance controls.
[Learn more](https://auth0.com/financial-services)
- Authorize agent-driven transfers, trades, and payments
- Replace brittle rules with centralized authorization
- Scale automation without compliance stress

### Modernize workflows without rebuilding systems
Manual identity stitching creates risk. Auth0 enables more secure, automated workflows across providers while supporting accountability and HIPAA compliance.
[Learn more](https://auth0.com/healthcare)
- Automate patient data access more safely
- Cut dev time building custom compliance infrastructure
- Deploy autonomous workflows with a clear audit trail

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I give AI agents the right permissions without hardcoding?

Hardcoding permissions is fast, but it fragments control and slows scale. [Auth0 lets agents](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/user-authentication) act more securely on behalf of users with centralized authorization. Policies evolve without code changes, and each action is auditable.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/call-your-apis-on-users-behalf)

### Can I treat AI agents like regular users?

Not exactly. Agents act continuously and across multiple systems on behalf of many users. Roles multiply, accountability blurs, and traceability becomes tricky. Auth0 provides patterns for modelling agents distinctly, so each action is intentional and auditable.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/asynchronous-authorization)

### What happens if authorization lives outside the identity layer?

Authorization in downstream services or app code works temporarily but fails at scale. Every new capability increases surface area and drift. Auth0 centralizes authorization in the identity layer, keeping policies consistent, adaptive, and auditable.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/get-started/authorization-for-rag)

### How does Auth0 help move AI agents from pilot to production?

By combining secure identity, [fine-grained authorization](https://auth0.com/fine-grained-authorization), and centralized control, Auth0 enables agents to act safely and autonomously at scale. Teams ship faster, reduce rework, and gain confidence in every deployment.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/overview)

### Can Auth0 integrate with my existing systems and APIs?

Yes. Auth0 works with any AI agent or application that makes API calls, including first-party APIs, external services, and third-party AI platforms. Integration is seamless and maintains auditability across your stack.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/get-started/overview)

### How does Auth0 help ensure AI agents comply with privacy and security standards?

AI agents often handle sensitive user data, making compliance critical. Auth0 enforces fine-grained authorization, audit trails, and identity verification for agent actions, helping you meet your regulatory requirements like GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/docs/secure/data-privacy-and-compliance)

### Can AI agents securely access multiple applications or APIs?

Yes. Auth0 enables cross-app and cross-service access for AI agents while enforcing centralized policies. Agents can request only the data and actions they need, reducing risk and maintaining traceable, auditable access across your stack.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/intro/call-others-apis-on-users-behalf)

### How do I scale AI agent deployments without increasing security risk?

Scaling agents can quickly increase your attack surface if authorization isn’t centralized. Auth0 moves identity and permissions into the [platform](https://auth0.com/platform) so that new agents can onboard quickly, policies can evolve automatically, and teams can retain complete oversight and auditability.\n\n[Read the docs](https://auth0.com/ai/docs/get-started/overview)

# Introduction

> The Git forge for agent-human collaboration

Entire brings your code, agent sessions, and team decisions together so people and agents can build on each other's work. You can host repositories close to where your agents run and preserve the context behind every change. Entire also has Continuous Memory that maps how your code connects with entire-graph and brings past sessions, documentation, and saved decisions together with entire-brain, so each new session can build on what your team has already learned, even when you switch agents and with Trails you can connect the idea to the implementation. Trails have agent reviews, CI results, and human approvals to help you merge with collaborate and review easily.

[Introducing Entire: the Git forge for agent human collaboration](https://www.youtube.com/embed/VFCRvJkgnxA)

## Set Up Entire

Start with the CLI and your coding agent, then bring your work, reviews, and project memory together.

> [card] [Install the Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.com/installation.md)
>
> Install the CLI to bring session capture and collaboration into your Git workflow.

> [card] [Connect Your Coding Agent](https://docs.entire.com/agents/setup.md)
>
> Set up Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or another supported agent to capture the context behind your code.

> [card] [Capture Your First Checkpoint](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/capture-checkpoints.md)
>
> Make a change with your agent and commit it to save the prompts, tool calls, and decisions alongside your code.

> [card] [Make Your First Commit with Trails](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/overview.md#create-a-trail)
>
> Create a Trail, link your branch, and commit your first change. Follow the work through agent reviews, CI checks, and human approvals before merging.

> [card] [Remember Everything with Continuous Memory](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview.md#before-you-start)
>
> Set up entire-brain and entire-graph to bring code context, past sessions, and saved decisions into project memory your agents can reuse.

## What Entire Does

> [card] [Code Hosting](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/overview.md)
>
> Host repositories directly on Entire's distributed Git network or mirror existing GitHub repositories in the regions closest to your agents.

> [card] [Entire Trails](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/overview.md)
>
> Plan work with people and agents, then follow it through review and merge. A Trail brings the intended outcome together with changes across repositories and branches, agent sessions, review findings, CI results, and human approvals. Set gates to define when each change is ready to merge.

> [card] [Continuous Integration](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/overview.md)
>
> Connect Buildkite or Depot to run builds and tests on push, review results on Trails, and require checks before merging. CI integrations are available in public preview.

> [card] [Session Storage](https://docs.entire.com/guides/sessions/overview.md)
>
> Commits made during an agent session are linked to checkpoints: the code change paired with the prompts, responses, and tool calls behind it. Review how a change happened, trace its origin, or resume work with its context intact.

> [card] [Agentic Search](https://docs.entire.com/guides/search/overview.md)
>
> Search repositories, commits, and agent sessions in one query. Give agents the implementation they need and the reasoning behind it, without retracing old work.

> [card] [Semantic Graph](https://docs.entire.com/guides/graph/overview.md)
>
> entire-graph maps the symbols and relationships in your code so agents find answers fast, cutting token spend by up to 71%.

> [card] [Continuous Memory](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview.md)
>
> entire-brain brings sessions, checkpoints, documentation, code context, and saved decisions into shared project memory. Give your next agent the lessons from earlier work, even when you switch agents.

> [card] [Dispatches](https://docs.entire.com/guides/dispatches/overview.md)
>
> Turn recent agent work into shareable updates across repositories. Summarize sessions, checkpoints, and commits for team updates, reviews, and handoffs without opening every conversation.

> [card] [Any Agent](https://docs.entire.com/agents/overview.md)
>
> Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity CLI, and more. Our open-source, MIT-licensed CLI captures sessions from any supported agent, and the Agent Integration Protocol adds others.

## Why Host Your Code With Entire

Coding agents create much more Git traffic than a typical human workflow. They clone repositories, inspect history, create worktrees, and run tasks in parallel.

Entire provides distributed Git hosting so agents can work from repositories close to where they run. It is up to 89x faster than the competition. You can mirror an existing GitHub repository into one or more Entire regions while keeping GitHub as the upstream source of truth, allowing your agents to clone and pull in parallel. And with Entire-native branches, you can continue pushing even during a GitHub outage, so you and your agents work is not interrupted.

This helps with:

* giving agents faster access to code and Git history
* supporting many concurrent agent workflows
* keeping code in the regions you choose
* continuing working with [Entire-native branches](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/entire-native-branches.md) when an upstream provider is unavailable

## Why Store Your Sessions with Entire

A diff doesn't clearly explain why a change was made. It does not show the request that started the work, the files an agent inspected, the commands it ran, or the decisions it made along the way. As massive amounts of AI-generated code are created, developers, teams and agents themselves struggle to link the intent back to the code change itself.

Entire captures that missing context and connects it to your Git history. You can use it to:

* review agent work before merging
* trace code back to the prompt and session that created it
* understand why an earlier team or agent chose a particular approach
* resume or hand off work with its context intact
* search prior work instead of understanding it from scratch

Taken together, Entire represents one API for your code and the context that created it. A new system of record for agentic coding.

## How It Works

1. Install the Entire CLI in your repository.
2. Connect Entire to the coding agent you use.
3. [Host your repository directly on Entire](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/repository.md) or [mirror an existing GitHub repository](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors.md) in the region closest to your agents, and point your Git remote at it.
4. Entire captures sessions and checkpoints as the agent works, and agents clone and push through your Entire remote.
5. Continue coding with your agent, enabling it with faster clones and the history behind your work.

## What Do You Want to Do?

> [card] [Understand Why Code Changed](https://docs.entire.com/learn/investigate-why-code-exists.md)
>
> Trace a line of code back to the agent session and decisions that produced it.

> [card] [Mirror a GitHub Repository](https://docs.entire.com/learn/mirror-a-github-repository.md)
>
> Create a regional mirror so agents clone and fetch from the region you choose.

> [card] [Find Previous Decisions](https://docs.entire.com/learn/search-past-agent-work.md)
>
> Search sessions, commits, prompts, and files.

> [card] [Review Agent Work Before You Merge](https://docs.entire.com/learn/review-and-recap-agent-work.md)
>
> Catch issues across agent-generated changes with recap and review.

# Introduction

> The Git forge for agent-human collaboration

Entire brings your code, agent sessions, and team decisions together so people and agents can build on each other's work. You can host repositories close to where your agents run and preserve the context behind every change. Entire also has Continuous Memory that maps how your code connects with entire-graph and brings past sessions, documentation, and saved decisions together with entire-brain, so each new session can build on what your team has already learned, even when you switch agents and with Trails you can connect the idea to the implementation. Trails have agent reviews, CI results, and human approvals to help you merge with collaborate and review easily.

[Introducing Entire: the Git forge for agent human collaboration](https://www.youtube.com/embed/VFCRvJkgnxA)

## Set Up Entire

Start with the CLI and your coding agent, then bring your work, reviews, and project memory together.

> [card] [Install the Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.com/installation.md)
>
> Install the CLI to bring session capture and collaboration into your Git workflow.

> [card] [Connect Your Coding Agent](https://docs.entire.com/agents/setup.md)
>
> Set up Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or another supported agent to capture the context behind your code.

> [card] [Capture Your First Checkpoint](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/capture-checkpoints.md)
>
> Make a change with your agent and commit it to save the prompts, tool calls, and decisions alongside your code.

> [card] [Make Your First Commit with Trails](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/overview.md#create-a-trail)
>
> Create a Trail, link your branch, and commit your first change. Follow the work through agent reviews, CI checks, and human approvals before merging.

> [card] [Remember Everything with Continuous Memory](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview.md#before-you-start)
>
> Set up entire-brain and entire-graph to bring code context, past sessions, and saved decisions into project memory your agents can reuse.

## What Entire Does

> [card] [Code Hosting](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/overview.md)
>
> Host repositories directly on Entire's distributed Git network or mirror existing GitHub repositories in the regions closest to your agents.

> [card] [Entire Trails](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/overview.md)
>
> Plan work with people and agents, then follow it through review and merge. A Trail brings the intended outcome together with changes across repositories and branches, agent sessions, review findings, CI results, and human approvals. Set gates to define when each change is ready to merge.

> [card] [Continuous Integration](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/overview.md)
>
> Connect Buildkite or Depot to run builds and tests on push, review results on Trails, and require checks before merging. CI integrations are available in public preview.

> [card] [Session Storage](https://docs.entire.com/guides/sessions/overview.md)
>
> Commits made during an agent session are linked to checkpoints: the code change paired with the prompts, responses, and tool calls behind it. Review how a change happened, trace its origin, or resume work with its context intact.

> [card] [Agentic Search](https://docs.entire.com/guides/search/overview.md)
>
> Search repositories, commits, and agent sessions in one query. Give agents the implementation they need and the reasoning behind it, without retracing old work.

> [card] [Semantic Graph](https://docs.entire.com/guides/graph/overview.md)
>
> entire-graph maps the symbols and relationships in your code so agents find answers fast, cutting token spend by up to 71%.

> [card] [Continuous Memory](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview.md)
>
> entire-brain brings sessions, checkpoints, documentation, code context, and saved decisions into shared project memory. Give your next agent the lessons from earlier work, even when you switch agents.

> [card] [Dispatches](https://docs.entire.com/guides/dispatches/overview.md)
>
> Turn recent agent work into shareable updates across repositories. Summarize sessions, checkpoints, and commits for team updates, reviews, and handoffs without opening every conversation.

> [card] [Any Agent](https://docs.entire.com/agents/overview.md)
>
> Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity CLI, and more. Our open-source, MIT-licensed CLI captures sessions from any supported agent, and the Agent Integration Protocol adds others.

## Why Host Your Code With Entire

Coding agents create much more Git traffic than a typical human workflow. They clone repositories, inspect history, create worktrees, and run tasks in parallel.

Entire provides distributed Git hosting so agents can work from repositories close to where they run. It is up to 89x faster than the competition. You can mirror an existing GitHub repository into one or more Entire regions while keeping GitHub as the upstream source of truth, allowing your agents to clone and pull in parallel. And with Entire-native branches, you can continue pushing even during a GitHub outage, so you and your agents work is not interrupted.

This helps with:

* giving agents faster access to code and Git history
* supporting many concurrent agent workflows
* keeping code in the regions you choose
* continuing working with [Entire-native branches](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/entire-native-branches.md) when an upstream provider is unavailable

## Why Store Your Sessions with Entire

A diff doesn't clearly explain why a change was made. It does not show the request that started the work, the files an agent inspected, the commands it ran, or the decisions it made along the way. As massive amounts of AI-generated code are created, developers, teams and agents themselves struggle to link the intent back to the code change itself.

Entire captures that missing context and connects it to your Git history. You can use it to:

* review agent work before merging
* trace code back to the prompt and session that created it
* understand why an earlier team or agent chose a particular approach
* resume or hand off work with its context intact
* search prior work instead of understanding it from scratch

Taken together, Entire represents one API for your code and the context that created it. A new system of record for agentic coding.

## How It Works

1. Install the Entire CLI in your repository.
2. Connect Entire to the coding agent you use.
3. [Host your repository directly on Entire](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/repository.md) or [mirror an existing GitHub repository](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors.md) in the region closest to your agents, and point your Git remote at it.
4. Entire captures sessions and checkpoints as the agent works, and agents clone and push through your Entire remote.
5. Continue coding with your agent, enabling it with faster clones and the history behind your work.

> [card] [Mirror a GitHub Repository](https://docs.entire.com/learn/mirror-a-github-repository.md)
>
> Create a regional mirror so agents clone and fetch from the region you choose.

> [card] [Find Previous Decisions](https://docs.entire.com/learn/search-past-agent-work.md)
>
> Search sessions, commits, prompts, and files.

> [card] [Review Agent Work Before You Merge](https://docs.entire.com/learn/review-and-recap-agent-work.md)
>
> Catch issues across agent-generated changes with recap and review.

# TypeScript AI Framework for Agents and Apps

Ship AI agents that reason, remember, and act in TypeScript. Mastra provides memory, tools, MCP, and observability to go from prototype to production.

Build agents that do the work, not just answer questions. Mastra is an open-source TypeScript framework for agents and workflows: connect models to your tools and data, give agents memory, and keep people involved when a task needs judgment.

Start with a single agent. Add workflows for steps that need a defined sequence, a harness for long-running work, and evals to measure whether your changes make the agent better.

Create a project:

```sh
npm create mastra@latest
```

Follow the [documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs.md) to configure your first agent. If you're a local coding agent with filesystem access, install the skills to get up-to-date guidance:

```sh
npx skills add mastra-ai/skills
```

## Agent framework

- **Agents**: choose a model, write instructions, and connect tools so your agent can act on your systems, not just generate text. [Agent documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/overview.md)
- **Workflows**: define typed steps, branches, and retries for processes that need predictable control flow. Pause for human input and resume when a decision is made. [Workflow documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs/workflows/overview.md)
- **Harness**: manage long-running work with persistent sessions, plan-and-build modes, tool approvals, and subagents. Send updates through Signals while an agent works. These are the primitives behind Mastra Code.
- **Memory**: retain useful context across conversations with observational memory, semantic recall, and thread storage. [Memory documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/overview.md)
- **Server**: expose agents and workflows through API endpoints. Develop locally, then deploy on your own infrastructure or Mastra Platform.
- **Factory**: coordinate coding agents from issue investigation through implementation and pull request review, with checkpoints for your team. [Mastra Factory](https://mastra.ai/factory)

## Observability

See what happened in a run, then test whether a change fixes it. Mastra pairs observability with evals and datasets so you can move from debugging individual failures to checking behavior across repeatable test cases.

- **Evals**: score agent output and behavior with code-based checks or model-based judges. Compare changes before shipping them. [Evals documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs/evals/overview.md)
- **Metrics**: track latency, token usage, and cost to understand where time and money go.
- **Datasets**: turn real inputs and expected outputs into versioned test cases. Run experiments to compare models, prompts, and agent configurations.
- **Tracing**: follow model calls, tool calls, and workflow steps to see where a run went wrong. [Tracing documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs/observability/tracing/overview.md)

[Observability documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs/observability/overview.md)

## Use cases

Build agents for your customers, your team, or your development process. Connect the tools and data each job requires, and decide which actions need human approval.

- **Customer support**: answer product questions from your documentation, investigate account issues, and prepare actions for a support team to approve.
- **Company knowledge**: search internal documents and connected data sources, then answer questions with references to the evidence.
- **Research assistants**: investigate a topic, compare sources, follow up on gaps, and produce a report others can verify.
- **Data analysis**: turn questions into database queries, analyze CSV files, and summarize the results.
- **Document processing**: extract structured data from PDFs and invoices, check it against existing records, and flag exceptions for review.
- **Coding agents**: investigate issues, plan changes, edit code, run tests, and review pull requests.
- **Incident response**: gather logs and deployment context, investigate likely causes, and propose next steps for an engineer to approve.
- **Customer feedback analysis**: find recurring problems across support conversations and customer feedback, then turn them into a product brief.
- **Team assistants**: bring work into Slack or other messaging channels, prepare daily briefings, and follow up on unfinished tasks.

Every documentation page is available as markdown. The index is at [`/llms.txt`](https://mastra.ai/llms.txt).

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Mastra?

Mastra is an open-source TypeScript framework for building AI-powered applications and agents. Mastra provides agents, workflows, memory, workspaces and observability, letting developers go from idea to implementation. Mastra integrates with frontend and backend frameworks like React, Next.js and Node, or can be deployed anywhere as a standalone server.

### Is Mastra an agent builder?

Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI agents and AI-powered applications. Mastra agents use LLMs and tools to solve open-ended tasks, reasoning about goals, deciding which tools to use and iterating internally until the model emits a final answer or an optional stopping condition is met. Mastra also provides workflows, memory, workspaces and observability to support the full agent development lifecycle.

### What can you build with Mastra?

Mastra supports building AI-powered applications that combine language understanding, reasoning and action to solve real-world tasks. Mastra use cases include conversational agents for customer support, onboarding or internal queries, domain-specific copilots for coding, legal, finance, research or creative work, workflow automations that trigger, route and complete multi-step processes, and decision-support tools that analyze data and provide actionable recommendations.

### What AI models and providers does Mastra support?

Mastra's model routing connects to 90+ providers through one standard interface. Mastra supports models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and more, allowing developers to use different AI providers through a single API.

### What are Mastra workflows?

Mastra's graph-based workflow engine orchestrates complex multi-step processes with explicit control over execution. Mastra workflows use an intuitive syntax for control flow including .then(), .branch() and .parallel() methods. Mastra workflows also support human-in-the-loop functionality, allowing developers to suspend a workflow and await user input or approval before resuming. Mastra uses storage to remember execution state, so workflows can pause indefinitely and resume where they left off.

### How does Mastra handle agent memory and context?

Mastra's memory system provides conversation history, data retrieval from APIs, databases and files, and human-like working and semantic memory so agents behave coherently. Developers can give Mastra agents the right context at the right time by combining message history with retrieval from external data sources.

### Does Mastra support MCP servers?

Mastra supports authoring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, exposing agents, tools and other structured resources via the MCP interface. MCP servers built with Mastra can be accessed by any system or agent that supports the protocol.

### How does Mastra handle testing and observability?

Mastra includes built-in scorers and observability tools to observe, measure and refine agent performance continuously. Mastra supports evaluating agent output using model-graded, rule-based and statistical methods, with custom evals to track agent performance over time. Mastra's observability features trace agent calls and token usage with support for external observability platforms. Mastra also provides guardrails to process inputs and outputs, helping prevent prompt injection and sanitize responses.

### How do you deploy Mastra applications?

Mastra applications can be deployed to any Node.js-compatible environment. Mastra includes optional built-in deployers for Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare to automate the deployment process. Developers can also deploy Mastra as a standalone server powered by Hono, integrate it with existing web frameworks like Next.js, or use their existing Hono, Express, Fastify or any other server app.

### Why use Mastra instead of a Python AI framework?

Mastra is purpose-built for TypeScript and designed around established AI patterns, giving TypeScript developers everything they need to build AI applications out of the box. Mastra bundles agents and workflows directly into existing React, Next.js and Node.js apps, or ships them as standalone endpoints. Mastra provides a complete set of AI primitives including workflows, agents, workspaces and observability in one modular framework.

### Is Mastra open source?

Mastra's core framework is open source under the Apache 2.0 license. Enterprise features are source-available under the Mastra Enterprise License. Mastra is free to start with no seats or usage tiers.

## Plan Feature Details

**Throughput** is the guaranteed number of successful searches per hour for your plan. To improve performance, distribute your searches evenly throughout the hour and across multiple hours.

**U.S. Legal Shield** provides up to $2 million in coverage for the scraping and parsing of search engine data, as long as your use of the data or service is not illegal.

**ZeroTrace Mode** prevents search data from being stored on our systems. When enabled, we do not retain search parameters, queries, or results, and each request is discarded after completion, reducing traceability and supporting privacy and compliance requirements.

## FAQs

### How are searches counted?

Only successful searches are counted toward your monthly searches. Cached, errored, and failed searches are not. The number of results returned per response will not affect the number of credits used—responses with 100 results or empty result sets will both count as 1 search.

### Can we upgrade, downgrade, or cancel at any time?

Yes, you can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel your plan at any time without any restrictions.

### What happens if I cancel before my plan expires?

If you cancel before your plan expires, you can continue to use your remaining searches until the renewal date. After that, your plan will not be renewed.

### What happens when I upgrade my plan?

When you upgrade your plan, you'll only pay the difference between your current plan and the new one. Your renewal date will remain the same.

### What happens when I downgrade my plan?

When you downgrade your plan, you'll keep your current renewal date, and your subscription will renew at the lower plan rate. Any remaining searches from your previous plan will be added to your 'Extra Credits' balance.

### What happens if I run out of searches in a month?

You can set your plan to Automatic Early Renewal. It will trigger an early renewal once you've used all your searches. You can toggle the Automatic Early Renewal anytime by visiting [this page](https://serpapi.com/plan). You can also renew your plan manually. In both cases, your searches will be fully replenished, your renewal date will be updated, and your searches will reset at the start of the new billing cycle.

### What's your refund policy?

We offer a full refund within 7 days of the date you subscribed to a plan unless you've used more than 20% of your searches.

What is a .tech domain, and who is it for?

.tech is a Top-Level Domain (nTLD) for tech startups. It tells VCs, customers, and the world that your startup’s core is tech.

How do I get a .tech domain?

You can get it right here. Just scroll up and search for the domain you want in the search bar. Prefer a registrar? .tech is available on GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare, Domain.com, 1&1 Ionos, OVHCloud, and Network Solutions.

What’s Privacy Protection and do I need it?

When you register a domain, your contact information, like name, email, and registered address, shows up in the public WHOIS directory by default. Privacy Protection hides that and replaces it with generic details so your data stays private.

How do I purchase, enable or disable Privacy Protection?

If Privacy Protection is not included with your domain, you can purchase it during registration or later through your .tech or registrar control panel.

To enable or disable Privacy Protection, follow these steps:

- Log in to the .tech [control panel](http://manage.get.tech/customer) (visit the registrar website if you haven’t purchased through .tech)

- Go to your domain settings

- Find the Privacy Protection or WHOIS Privacy option

- Turn it on or off

- Save your changes

Does .tech offer hosting?

No, we don’t offer hosting.

How do I manage my domain name(s)?

To manage your domain name(s), log in to the .tech [control panel](http://manage.get.tech/customer) using the email ID and password you registered with. For step-by-step instructions, refer to [this guide](https://manage.get.tech/kb/servlet/KBServlet/cat119.html). If you bought your .tech domain from a registrar, check their website for information on how to manage your domain name(s) through their portal.

I got my .tech domain. What else do I need to set up a website?

Once you’ve got your .tech domain, connect it to your website by updating the name servers or A record with your hosting provider. You can do this through the .tech control panel or the control panel of the registrar you bought your domain from.

How do I add the name servers or A Records to the domain name?

If you bought your .tech domain directly from us, follow these steps:

- Log in to the .tech [control panel](http://manage.get.tech/customer)

- Search for your domain and go to the Order Information view

- Click on the Name Servers link

- Add up to 13 name servers and click Update

- If you bought your domain through a registrar, visit their website for steps on adding name servers or A records.

How can I set up a redirect?

You can redirect your website using the Domain Forwarding service.

To set up Domain Forwarding, follow these steps:

- Log in to the .tech [control panel](http://manage.get.tech/customer) and select your .tech domain

- Go to the Domain Forwarding section and click Manage Domain Forwarding

- Enter the destination URL and click Save

I have purchased a domain that I no longer require. How can I cancel my domain and get a refund?

Deleting a domain is permanent. It can’t be undone, and there are no refunds for the domain or any services linked to it.

To delete your domain, follow these steps:

- Log in to the .tech [control panel](http://manage.get.tech/customer), search for the domain, and open the Order Details view

- Click the Delete Order link

- Confirm the deletion on the next page

- Once you delete your domain, any connected websites, email accounts, or services will stop working and can’t be recovered.

I accidentally deleted my domain. How can I restore it?

Unfortunately, deleted domains can’t be restored. Deletion is permanent, and the domain is immediately lost. You can try registering the domain again, but note that availability is not guaranteed.

What happens if I forget to renew my domain and it expires?

If your .tech domain expires, here's what happens:

- Days 1-36: Renewal Grace Period

  Your domain stops working, but you can still renew it at the regular price.

- Days 37-66: Redemption Period

  You can restore your domain by paying a restoration fee and the renewal cost.

- Days 67-71: Pending Delete

  The domain is locked. You can’t renew or recover it.

- After Day 71: Publicly Available

  The domain is deleted and open for anyone to register. Popular domains may get snapped up instantly.

Best move? Renew early or for multiple years. It’s the easiest way to avoid losing your domain.

What do I do if I forget to renew my domain?

We send multiple reminders before your domain expires. Mandatory emails go out 30 and 7 days before expiry. You can also choose to get reminders on the 1st, 11th, and 21st day in the last 45 days. These can be managed from your .tech or registrar control panel.

If you miss the deadline, you have a 36-day Grace Period to renew your domain at the regular price. After that, your domain enters a 30-day Redemption Period. You can recover it, but the process includes a restoration fee.

For more information, refer to [this guide](https://manage.get.tech/kb/servlet/KBServlet/faq460.html).

Can I transfer my domain to another provider or registrar?

Yes, you can transfer your domain to another provider or registrar. Transfer charges apply. Before you begin, check that your domain is eligible. For detailed steps and eligibility checks, refer to [this guide](https://manage.get.tech/kb/servlet/KBServlet/faq556.html).

What’s a Premium domain? What’s a Reserved domain? Why do they cost more?

Premium domains are short, easy to remember, and often include popular keywords. They're priced higher—at varying costs—based on factors like character count, search demand, recall value, and potential to drive traffic.

Reserved domains are held back by the registry. This could be due to policy restrictions, sensitive terms, or internal use. These domain names may not be available for registration.

Want to check domain availability? Reach out to our support team at [support@get.tech](mailto:support@get.tech)

Who do I report abuse to?

To report abuse related to a .tech domain, fill out [this form](https://abuse.radix.website/).

Who do I contact for support?

For any support-related queries, send an email to [support@get.tech](mailto:support@get.tech)

## FAQ

### Is there a free tier available for MongoDB Atlas? What does it include?

Yes, MongoDB Atlas offers a free-forever tier, the M0. Atlas’s free tier includes 512 MB of storage, 32MB of sort memory, and up to 100 operations per second. The free tier is a great starting point to learn about MongoDB and explore its capabilities in a fully managed cloud environment.

[Get started with a free tier →](https://www.mongodb.com/cloud/atlas/register)  
[Atlas Free tier features and limitations →](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/free-shared-limitations/)  
[Guide: How to deploy a free tier cluster →](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/deploy-free-tier-cluster/)

### How do I choose the right cluster tier for my application?

Choosing the right MongoDB Atlas cluster tier for your application involves considering the application's workload, data size, and performance needs. Key considerations include:

- **Free Tier (M0):** Best for learning and exploring, with [limited resources](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/free-shared-limitations/).

- **Flex:** Ideal for development and testing, offering the lowest cost option with certain [feature limitations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/flex-limitations/#std-label-atlas-flex-limitations).

- **Dedicated (M10 & M20):** Suitable for pre-production and small, non-critical workloads. These tiers utilize shared vCPUs and support replica set deployments offering fully featured access to Atlas.

- **Dedicated (M30+):** Recommended for performance-critical and high-traffic workloads, supporting both replica sets and sharded clusters with fully featured access to Atlas with dedicated vCPUs.

Clusters can always be scaled up from any tier as requirements expand. If unsure, MongoDB recommends starting with a lower tier and [monitoring performance](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts/) before adjusting. For all Dedicated tiers, use auto-scaling to adjust cluster tier and storage as workloads evolve.

[How to select your cluster tier →](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-clusters/#select-cluster-tier)  
[Atlas cluster sizing and tier selection →](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/)  
[Learn more about dedicated clusters →](https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/dedicated-clusters)

### What factors influence my MongoDB Atlas costs?

MongoDB Atlas costs are based on a pay-as-you-go model, influenced by several key factors:

- **Cluster tier and type:** The selected tier is the foundational cost driver. Higher tiers provide more dedicated resources and capabilities.

- **Cloud provider and region:** Costs vary slightly across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, and between different geographic regions.

- **Data storage:** Includes the size of your data and indexes.

- **Data transfer (networking):** Charges mainly apply to data moving out of your Atlas cluster (egress) or between different regions/cloud providers. Inbound data transfers are typically free. Free and Flex tiers are not charged for outgoing data.

- **Backup services:** Costs are based on the region and the monthly storage consumed by snapshots and oplogs for continuous backups. Note that backup services are not available for the Free tier.

- **Add-on tools and services:** Additional add-on tools and services contribute to the overall cost. Examples include but are not limited to:

  - Atlas Stream Processing

  - Dedicated MongoDB Search on Atlas Nodes

  - Support subscriptions

  - Premium Atlas Charts features

Additional factors that can influence cost over time include:

- Fluctuations in usage

- Configuration adjustments

- Auto-scaling behavior

- New features

- Cloud provider price changes

[Atlas cluster configuration costs →](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/)  
[Understand Your MongoDB Invoice →](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/invoice-breakdown/#std-label-atlas-invoice-breakdown)

### How do I manage and reduce MongoDB Atlas costs?

**Right-size clusters:** Pause development or testing clusters when not in use. Alternatively, terminate them if no longer required. For Dedicated clusters, use [auto-scaling](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling/) to adjust cluster storage and/or tier based on real-time CPU and memory utilization.

**Optimize data management:** Design efficient [schemas](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/schema-design-process/) and use strategic [indexing](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes/) to improve query performance while minimizing resource consumption. Regularly review clusters, databases, and collections to eliminate duplication, outdated data, and unused sample datasets. For Dedicated clusters, use Atlas [Online Archive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/online-archive/manage-online-archive/) to tier infrequently accessed data, which will reduce primary storage costs.

**Minimize data transfer:** Reduce [data transfer costs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs/) by heeding the following best practices:

- Avoid queries that re-read client data or re-write existing cluster data.

- Use query projections to only retrieve necessary fields.

- Deploy applications in the same cloud region as the Atlas cluster.

- Enable network compression in client drivers to reduce data volume.

**Monitor & alerts:** Regularly review spending patterns using the [Billing Cost Explorer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/#billing-cost-explorer) tool in Atlas. Additionally, set up billing [alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts/#std-label-arch-center-monitoring-alerts-recs) to be notified of unexpected cost spikes or when usage approaches predefined thresholds.

[Billing breakdown and optimization →](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/billing-breakdown-optimization/)
